clue.text: Single fellow having lost heart becomes glum

parts.note: sole means single or only

indicators.note: a word that has lost its heart is missing its middle letter, here the word for fellow

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A bachelor who has had his heart broken turns gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' removes the middle A from MAN, leaving MN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a solemn face is a serious, unsmiling, gloomy one.

clue.text: Eccentric type, one with horse going around Welsh town

parts.note: a card is an amusing oddball
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: going around tells us the horse word turns back on itself

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: An oddball rides a horse round a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric type' reads as a description, but a card is a British word for an amusing oddball. Cardigan is a town on the west coast of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Cardigan is a market town on the west coast of Wales, which gave its name to the knitted jacket.

clue.text: Ruler always wanting gold intercepted by commoner

indicators.note: intercepted by means the always word is cut into by the commoner word

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
an MP is a member of the House of Commons
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A monarch who is forever lacking gold is waylaid by a peasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commoner' looks like a peasant but means a Member of Parliament in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an emperor is the sovereign ruler of an empire.

clue.text: Get married after end of engagement, as agreed

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word engagement

parts.note: allied means joined together, as in a marriage

explanation.surface: A couple wed once their engagement is over, as they had arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: figures that tallied matched up, corresponded or agreed.

clue.text: Wooden piece, a musical composition to be rejected

indicators.note: to be rejected means the composition is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: a nonet is a piece written for nine players

explanation.surface: A piece written for woodwind is turned down by the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry term: a tenon is the projecting wooden tongue that fits into a mortise joint.

clue.text: The Parisian, fit to join army officer as collaborator

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
le is French for the
an ague is a shivering fit

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, fit for duty, teams up with a colonel as his partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a colleague is someone who works alongside you, a fellow worker.

clue.text: Theft from ship below hidden in sand on French coast?

indicators.note: hidden in puts the below word inside the beach word

parts.note: plage is the French word for beach
under means below

explanation.surface: Loot taken from below decks of a ship is buried in the sand on a French beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'sand on French coast' must be translated: the French for beach. Plunderage is a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic term: plunderage is the embezzlement of goods on board a ship.

clue.text: Cell seen in Paris kept in order

indicators.note: kept in means the seen word is held inside the order abbreviation

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
vu is French for seen

explanation.surface: A prison cell visited in Paris is kept tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM (Order of Merit) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Biology: an ovum is a female egg cell.

clue.text: Combat vehicle has reversed direction — what's to be done?

indicators.note: reversing a compass direction swaps north for south, so one compass letter becomes its opposite

parts.note: a tank is an armoured fighting vehicle

explanation.surface: A tank has turned round on the battlefield: what now?
explanation.walkthrough: 'has reversed direction' swaps N (north) for its opposite S (south).
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: a task is a job, something that has to be done.

clue.text: Twenty clubs maybe providing sporting records

parts.note: a score is twenty
clubs is one suit of playing cards

explanation.surface: Twenty golf clubs might lead to some impressive sporting tallies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport: scorecards record the runs, strokes or points in a match.

clue.text: Attending trial, social worker is a witness

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a test is a trial
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A social worker present at a court case gives evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a welfare officer but an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal word: an attestant is one who attests, bearing witness to a signature or fact.

clue.text: This writer's needing work, giving hint

parts.note: the setter refers to themself; this writer is is I'm
to ply is to work at a trade

explanation.surface: An author who needs a job drops a heavy hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to suggest something without saying it outright.

clue.text: Putting up with noise when a giant maybe comes round

indicators.note: comes round means the giant phrase wraps around the noise word

parts.note: a giant is an example of something big
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Tolerating the racket when an ogre turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' puts DIN inside A BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal synonym: abiding a thing is tolerating or bearing it.

clue.text: Bird once something to eat for member of ancient tribe

parts.note: the moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: An extinct bird served as a meal for a tribesman of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical people: the Moabites lived in Moab, east of the Dead Sea.

clue.text: Tribal chief to flop down with Italian love

parts.note: to sag is to droop or flop
amore is Italian for love

explanation.surface: A chieftain collapses in a heap with his Italian sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: North American usage: a sagamore was a chief among some Algonquian peoples.

clue.text: Messenger coming with another message

indicators.note: coming with says the letters arrive carried inside the following words, spanning their join

explanation.surface: A courier turns up bearing yet another note.
explanation.walkthrough: The god sits across the join of 'another' and 'message', apt since he carried the gods' messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: the herald of the Olympian gods, with winged sandals, carried their errands to mortals.

clue.text: Confectionery leads to big belly? You find meat!

indicators.note: leads to says the confectionery comes first and is followed by the belly word

parts.note: sweets are confectionery
a pot is a pot belly

explanation.surface: Eating sweets gives you a paunch, while you look for real food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' is the sporting term for the best hitting part of a bat or racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport idiom: the meat of a bat is its ideal hitting area, the place where you find it.

clue.text: Plant at high level — it's nothing to climb to collect it

indicators.note: to collect it means the reversed nothing word gathers the height word inside
in a down clue, to climb means read from bottom to top, reversing the nothing word

parts.note: nil is nothing
up means at a height

explanation.surface: A plant growing high up, which you climb to gather.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to climb' means reading upwards; 'it's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Get soaked in awful rain, forced to go outside

indicators.note: to go outside means the forced word wraps around the jumbled rain

parts.note: made, as in made to do it, means forced

indicators.note: awful signals that the rain letters are jumbled

parts.note: fodder, as written

explanation.surface: Getting drenched in a downpour, made to go out into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' is a participle meaning compelled, as in 'made to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery: meat left to marinade steeps in a flavoured liquid, becoming soaked.

clue.text: What might be term for number? 'Rational' might, possibly

definitions.text: What might be term for number?

indicators.note: possibly signals the two words may be rearranged

parts.note: fodder, as written
fodder, as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about naming numbers: could 'rational' be the right term?
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RATIONAL plus MIGHT. 'Rational' is a decoy: a rational number is a real term but not the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics: the antilogarithm of a logarithm is the number it stands for, so it names that number.

clue.text: Monument shows oddly droll fellows

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of droll

parts.note: men are fellows

explanation.surface: A memorial depicts some comic chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeology: a dolmen is a prehistoric tomb of upright stones topped by a slab.

clue.text: Beating in examination

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the phrase: a violent assault and a thorough inspection.

clue.text: Exhibitionist perhaps receiving good poke in the ribs?

indicators.note: receiving means the exhibitionist word takes the good letter inside

parts.note: an exhibitionist may appear naked, so nude

explanation.surface: A streaker gets a jab in the side for his trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a gentle dig with the elbow to attract attention.

clue.text: Deliverer of successive hits? Gosh — unusually grand cheer goes round!

indicators.note: goes round means the jumbled letters surround the exclamation
unusually signals the grand cheer letters in a strange order

parts.note: fodder, as written
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: A cheer erupts at a big hit, and someone says 'Gosh!'
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is British slang meaning gosh. 'Hits' are hit records, not blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit records: an old record changer dropped one single after another onto the turntable.

clue.text: Out of bed with surroundings causing distress

parts.note: up means risen from bed
a setting is the surroundings of a place

explanation.surface: Getting up in such a place is distressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something upsetting troubles or disturbs you.

clue.text: Sort of food formula for apes?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer's second word turned to mush makes apes, so the answer is a recipe for that word

explanation.surface: A recipe for monkey food.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: MUSHY is an anagram signal working on PEAS, which give APES.
explanation.definitionFit: British side dish: a mash of marrowfat peas often served with fish and chips.

clue.text: A vet working with cat, I start operating

indicators.note: working signals the letters are set to work in a new order

parts.note: fodder, as written
fodder, as written

explanation.surface: A vet getting busy with a cat says 'I'll begin the operation.'
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges A VET, CAT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to set something in motion, switching it on.

clue.text: Heavy metal thus upset island wanting ambient silence

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the thus word upside down, reversing it

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: ambient means surrounding, so the silence word goes around the island letter

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum

explanation.surface: Heavy-metal fans upset an island that wants peace and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' turns a word upside down; 'wanting' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: osmium is the densest naturally occurring metallic element.

clue.text: For horses, a beastly disease that is to be avoided

indicators.note: to be avoided means the that-is letters are left out

parts.note: rabies is a disease spread by animal bites
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Horses need protection from an animal disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be avoided' removes IE from A RABIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Arabs are a prized breed of horse from the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Wheeled carriage carries one legendary king

indicators.note: carries means the carriage holds the one letter inside it

parts.note: a pram is a baby's wheeled carriage
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pushchair transports a mythical monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek legend: Priam was the king of Troy during the Trojan War.
